content: A disabled millennial expresses feeling fortunate to simply leave the house, highlighting a growing concern about loneliness among disabled individuals in Britain. New research from Scope reveals that nearly half of working-age disabled people experience chronic loneliness, totaling approximately 3 million people. This issue compounds the existing national problem, as Britain is labeled the "loneliness capital of Europe" with weakened social connections. While loneliness can exist even amidst company, the research underscores the profound isolation faced by disabled people in the country, signaling an epidemic of loneliness.
